lines: It names no group and no measurement, and a single person has one answer.
``How many pets do Summit Middle School students have at home?''
A statistic --- it describes the 60-member sample, not all 1,200 members.
Time or cost --- reaching every one of 1,200 members would take far too long.
Method 1. Response bias --- the leading wording pushes people toward yes, so it
overestimates: 78\% against 42\%, or 1,404 card holders against 756.
Reversed arrow: a B average is what lets a student run for office, so grades put
students into the officer group --- that pushes the officers' percent up on its own.
Leading --- ``Wouldn't it be great'' pushes toward yes, so the wording is not neutral.
Double-barrelled --- it asks about a scoreboard and the gym in one item.
A is observational, B is an experiment: who decided the groups --- students chose in A,
a generator assigned in B. Observing is how B collected data, not how it built groups.
Study B. Random assignment made the groups alike at the start, so the program is the
only difference left. Study A's bigger gap earns only ``is associated with.''
Students who chose to attend were already motivated, so A's program group started
ahead. Self-selection inflates the gap; in B nobody chose, so that head start is gone.
Nonresponse bias --- the 70\% who never returned it cared less about a garden.
It overestimates by 35 percentage points, or $720 - 405 = 315$ households.
Twice the responses, the same wrong 80\%: a larger sample does not remove bias.
Draw a random sample of households and follow up by phone or in person until nearly
all of them answer. That removes the nonresponse bias, which size never did.
Stratified. A full numbered list exists and the grades are expected to differ, so
drawing at random within each grade guarantees all three are represented in proportion.
Survey. The question has a fixed yes/no answer and needs many students, so a short
written instrument given to the whole sample can be counted quickly.
Chance never chose her advisory --- the other 695 students could not be asked --- so the
match is luck: the same room could have missed by 20 points and nothing would warn her.
She may say only that 36\% of her own advisory wants a Friday movie night.
